entries.title: Normalized Cardy crossing function
entries.statement: For 0<=u<=1, define C(u)=B(1/3,1/3)^(-1) times the integral from 0 to u of [s(1-s)]^(-2/3) ds, where B(1/3,1/3) is the same integral over [0,1]. This defines a function; invoking it as a square-lattice crossing limit requires a separate convergence theorem.

entries.title: DRAFT: two Cardy martingales identify a local SLE(6) driver
entries.statement: DRAFT conditional derivation, kept mathematically by independent referee w413 in REVIEW_PACKET.md on 2026-10-10; integration's served-model/different-model gate remains unestablished. This is not a square-bond percolation proof. Let W be a continuous adapted real driver with deterministic W(0) for chordal Loewner dg_t(z)=2/(g_t(z)-W_t)dt in a usual filtration. Choose W(0)<x1<x2<x3, with 0<X1<X2<X3 before swallowing, Xi=g_t(xi)-W_t. If BOTH C(X1/X2) and C(X1/X3) are continuous local martingales in the SAME filtration throughout a locally stopped lifetime, then W-W(0) is a continuous local martingale with quadratic variation 6t over that lifetime. Invert the first observable to make W a semimartingale; Ito gives dA=(1/Xi+1/Xj)(2dt-dV/3), where A is the driver drift measure and V its local-martingale quadratic variation. Subtract the two identities to force dV=6dt and dA=0. Square-lattice conditional Cardy limits and trace convergence remain unproved here; retain concept/draft status until the remaining promotion gate passes.
assumptions: Usual filtration and a continuous adapted Loewner driver.
Three ordered, positive, surviving boundary distances.
Both specified Cardy observables are local martingales in the same filtration.
Conclusion only over a lifetime covered by localized observable hypotheses.

entries.title: DRAFT: one Cardy martingale admits a deterministic driver
entries.statement: DRAFT explicit obstruction kept mathematically by independent referee w413 on 2026-10-10; integration's served-model/different-model gate remains unestablished. This is a counterexample to a general inference, not to the percolation conjecture. For 0<=t<1/2, set Y=sqrt(4-8t), W=3-3Y/2, g_t(1)=3-Y and g_t(2)=3-Y/2. The real Loewner equations hold: g_t(1)'=2/(Y/2) and g_t(2)'=2/Y. Their distances from W have ratio 1/2, so the single Cardy observable C((g_t(1)-W)/(g_t(2)-W)) is the constant martingale 1/2. W is nonconstant deterministic finite variation with zero quadratic variation, so one such observable cannot identify a Brownian driver without further premises. For a third mark starting at 3, the initial ratio derivative is -2/27, and its Cardy observable is not a martingale.
assumptions: C is the normalized beta-integral crossing function.

entries.title: Square-bond percolation: conditional observable identification gap
entries.statement: The unproved input in the w412 Cardy-martingale route is identification of TWO actual discrete crossing or boundary-order Doob martingales, including their induced primal/dual boundary conditions after exploration, with joint limits C(X1/X2) and C(X1/X3) in the SAME limiting exploration filtration on random slit domains. Exact discrete martingale identities alone do not identify their limiting functions. Fixed-domain crossing estimates, RSW tightness and large-scale rotational invariance do not alone supply this stated input. Joint convergence must retain the past-versus-future martingale identities; an enlarged filtration and discontinuous boundary stopping times require their own checks. No square-lattice conformal-invariance result is asserted by this draft.
assumptions: Application under discussion is critical independent square-lattice bond percolation at p=1/2.
This is a proof-gap record for the specific conditional-observable route, not a claim that it is the only possible route.

entries.title: C0017: historical source and unverified current proof claims
entries.statement: C0017 asks for Cardy crossing limits and SLE(6) exploration limits for critical independent bond percolation on the square lattice at p=1/2. Garban-Steif arXiv:1102.5761v3, Chapter II section 4, printed p.24 / PDF page 26, calls its conformal invariance an open problem in 2012; the adjacent established Theorem II.2 concerns triangular-lattice site percolation. A bounded 2026-10-10 primary search also found square-bond proof claims arXiv:1112.2017v5 and arXiv:2409.03235v6, without independently checking their mathematics. Thus the task records current openness as UNKNOWN and makes no novelty claim. Historical source wording, an arXiv abstract, a source hash, or an ingestion receipt is not an independent mathematical proof certificate.
assumptions: Bounded search and source-recovery evidence only; no soundness judgment of the claimed square-bond proofs.
